title: Transport for the Malta trip (13–19 October 2026)
intro: Start with current organizer instructions and the visible dated agenda; only 14–16 October entries were visible in the 11 October Eventbrite read. The current direct Eventbrite extraction did not expose a Thunderpick-specific ticket price, booking fee, reservation action or checkout; a generic ‘Free / Oct 14–18 / Reserve a spot’ recommendation card is not attributable to the event, and the secondary HLTV report is not a current checkout quote. The traveler’s reservation, gate and 17–18 October agenda remain unconfirmed. Route 186 and Route 214 are public-bus candidates, not confirmed hotel-to-gate journeys. A fresh full read of the static Route 186 page separates the two Stadium stops: outbound from Qawra runs via Stadium 6227 toward Rabat through about 22:08, while the opposite return at Stadium 2194 toward Buġibba is displayed through 20:53 and terminates at Buġibba Bay 1, not Qawra. The static table is not date-specific; do not use 22:04/22:08 as a return time. Run the dated planner in both directions and check the onward Buġibba-to-Qawra link. MPT publishes seasonal single prices (€2.50 summer / €2.00 winter) and card products; its stated winter range ends 13 June 2026, while third-party 2026 guides suggest the 18/19 October boundary. That trip-date fare assignment is a partially verified inference, not an operator confirmation. Keep a live-quote taxi/ride-hailing alternative for late finishes, especially on 17 October. The 17 October diversion and separate Saqqajja closure are recorded below; neither is a saved journey.

In the Buġibba-bound direction the page's later window shows Rabat 2 (2569) departures 16:45–20:45 and Stadium 2194 at 16:55–20:53, with the same journey reaching Buġibba Bay 1 (2527) at 21:27 — a 34-minute run from Stadium 2194 to the terminus for the 20:53 boarding. records.description: Route 186 runs between Rabat and Buġibba and is an operator- and venue-endorsed link from Qawra to the Ta’ Qali Stadium stop. Direction matters: the outbound direction serves Qawra seafront stops (Arznell 950, Luzzu 951, Qawra 952), continues via Ta’ Qali Stadium 6227 and heads toward Rabat. The return from opposite-side Stadium stop 2194 heads toward Buġibba, lists no Il-Qawra stop and ends at Buġibba Bay 1 (2527). Two full-page reads (11 and 12 October 2026) both display the 2194 Buġibba-bound row through 20:53 and the outbound 6227 series later (about 22:04/22:08): the later figures are outbound-side readings, not a late return. The operator now labels the route “Scheduled Frequency every 30 minutes”, which matches the :23/:53 pattern visible at Stadium 2194 in the later window (for example 20:23 and 20:53); the 20:53 row reaches Buġibba Bay 1 at 21:27. The page does not label rows by the traveler’s date or service day, so 20:53 is a static-table observation, not a guaranteed trip-date last bus. Confirm the actual date, both stop sides, walks and onward Buġibba-to-Qawra leg in the MPT planner; no door-to-door journey is saved.
records.notes: Direct full-page reads of the Malta Public Transport Route 186 page on 11 and 12 October 2026: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ . The 12 October read reproduces the operator's own frequency label (“Scheduled Frequency every 30 minutes”, Monday–Friday/Saturday/Sunday tabs), the Buġibba-bound sequence (Rabat 2 2569 → Mdina 135 → Saqqajja 4627 → Stadium 2194 → Ħ’Attard → Mosta → Burmarrad → St Paul's Bay → Buġibba Moll 6193 → Buġibba Bay 1 2527 terminus), the displayed 16:55–20:53 window at Stadium 2194 and the 21:27 arrival at Buġibba Bay 1 for the 20:53 boarding. Toward Buġibba, stops from Gholja 2 (1101) through Targa (1138) will not be served; those are Mosta-corridor stops about four minutes upstream of the Ta' Qali Stadium stop, so the Stadium boarding stop and the Qawra seafront stops are not in the omitted span. records.notes: Operator wording read in full 11 October 2026 at https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ and repeated in the Route 186 page's service-update panel at https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ . Exact wording: "Detour in effect weekly on Friday, Saturday from 7:00 PM to 12:00 AM, starting October 17. Detour ends October 18 at approximately 12:00 AM. Toward Bugibba, stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served." **Date scope:** because the notice itself begins on 17 October (a Saturday), the Friday 16 October evening runs before this diversion starts and the Saturday 17 October evening, 19:00–00:00, is inside it. The same cluster covers Routes 202, 260, 47, 103, 45, 405, 238 and the 203/280/31/41/42/48/N48 group, all reading the same 17-October Friday/Saturday 19:00–00:00 window; Route 405 omits Rotunda 1 and Bezzina, 47 omits Gatt through Rotunda 1, 45/103/202/260/280/31/41/42/48/N48 omit their own Mosta–Rotunda segments. A fourth read of the full three-chunk updates page at this check found **no** Thunderpick World Championship, BLAST Arena Studios, Ta' Qali event or TQ-numbered service notice, and the same page also lists the Saqqajja stop closure (ID 4627) until approximately 1 January plus weekday construction detours on other routes (including 54/106 toward Attard on 13 October and a 46/260 Monday–Thursday 21:00–05:00 detour starting 12 October). Re-read 12 October 2026 across three chunks of the live feed: both Route 186 notices and the full dated cluster remain published, including the “starting October 17” wording; the rest of that read is catalogued in the trip-week notices record. Both operator pages re-read 12 October 2026 confirm the dated notice is still printed exactly as quoted above and that the older 20:00–00:00 notice remains displayed beside it; the comparison between the two is unchanged, so Friday 16 October still sits before the dated diversion and Saturday 17 October 19:00–00:00 sits inside it.

TQ2, TQ3 and TQ4 are also listed in the operator's route directory. The corridor and the event-only nature of these routes are documented by a public route list, which describes special one-off services organised after major events such as festivals and concerts, announced a few days beforehand, and gives TQ1 as Ta' Qali → Rabat, Mosta, Naxxar, St. Paul's Bay, Qawra → Buġibba: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_bus_routes_in_Malta . A 2023 operator announcement for a Ta' Qali festival gives the same four TQ corridors with 23:15, 00:15, 01:15 and 02:15 departures: https://newsbook.com.mt/en/malta-public-transport-provides-special-service-for-earth-garden-2023/ . NO TWC-specific special service was found on 11 Oct 2026 and none is assumed. Monitor https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ and the tallinja app; if nothing is announced, recheck the date-specific planner and compare a live ride quote only if no suitable public-service return is confirmed. Current integration recheck read route-page chunks 0 and 6, including the final “Timetable not available!” message. The intervening all-network stop selector was not read; it is not a TQ1 stop list. Historical route/report evidence was not freshly re-opened. Re-opened again later on 11 October 2026: the TQ1 page still ended with 'Timetable not available!', and the operator's full latest-service-updates page read at the same check published no TQ service and no Thunderpick/BLAST event notice. Two days before the event this remains the single most useful thing to recheck daily, because a TQ service through Qawra is a published corridor that could provide another potential return option if a trip-specific service is announced. Third read on 11 October 2026 added two published route definitions and one dated precedent, still without any Thunderpick announcement. The route definitions come from the Wikipedia list of Maltese bus routes' special-services table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_bus_routes_in_Malta): 'TQ1 (Northern Route) | Ta' Qali | via Rabat, Mosta, Naxxar, St. Paul's Bay, Qawra | Buġibba' and 'TQ2 (Central Route) | Ta' Qali | via Lija, Birkirkara (Bypass), San Ġwann, St Julian's, Sliema | Valletta'; a 2023 Earth Garden special-service report used the same two route names and stop sequences (https://newsbook.com.mt/en/malta-public-transport-provides-special-service-for-earth-garden-2023/). The precedent is MPT's own announced 2026 national-stadium service: for the Malta v Luxembourg play-off it ran extra trips on key routes from Valletta, Buġibba, Sliema and the University, made regular and special services free for Tallinja card holders, charged €2 on board for everyone else, and stationed buses close to the stadium after the final whistle departing to Valletta, Sliema, St Paul's Bay, Żurrieq and Paola 'depending on demand' (https://lovinmalta.com/news/local/malta-public-transport-to-run-special-bus-services-for-malta-vs-luxembourg-play-off/). That is a news report about a March 2026 football match, not a published TWC service: it shows the Ta' Qali post-event Bus-and-Buġibba pattern exists when MPT chooses to run it, and nothing more. The 11 October three-chunk re-read of the operator's updates page still contained no TWC, BLAST or TQ notice, so the late-return question stays open and any special service would be announced only days beforehand. Rechecked 12 October 2026: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/TQ1/ still prints “Timetable not available!”, and a full three-chunk read of the operator's latest-service-updates feed on the same day (https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ ) still carries no TQ-numbered, BLAST, Thunderpick or Ta' Qali event service. One day before the trip window opens, no special-service timetable exists to plan against.

records.description: A three-chunk read of the operator's latest-service-updates feed on 11 October 2026. It confirms the 17–18 October detour cluster already on file and sets out in full two dated notices that existed in this project only as a passing mention inside the 17 October diversion record: the Mon–Thu night detour on Routes 46/260 running 12–16 October, and the Tuesday 13 October daytime Attard detours on Routes 54/106. What is new here is the stop-level detail and its own record and page entry — not the first observation of the notices. Nothing on the page is event-specific to the CS2 tournament, and no TQ-numbered service is published. Whether any notice changes a particular Qawra ↔ Ta' Qali journey still has to be settled in the operator's date-specific planner: the rows print no year, and the route pages carry unlabelled timetable variants. Route identities are quoted from the notices; the notices do not say which streets the diverted buses take.
records.notes: Three chunks read end to end on 11 October 2026: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . The same notices were already summarised inside the record route-186-oct17-detour, whose notes read 11 October 2026 state: 'the same page also lists the Saqqajja stop closure (ID 4627) until approximately 1 January plus weekday construction detours on other routes (including 54/106 toward Attard on 13 October and a 46/260 Monday–Thursday 21:00–05:00 detour starting 12 October)'. This record expands that mention rather than superseding it. Corridor context: the Route 186 timetable and notice panel https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ and the date-specific planner https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ — no journey was saved. The TQ1 page re-read the same day still prints 'Timetable not available!': https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/TQ1/ . The feed is live and can gain an event notice days before departure, so check it daily during 13–19 October. Route 260 is named in both the 17–18 October cluster and the Mon–Thu night notice; whether either touches a stop this traveller would use is not established by the notice text. Re-read 12 October 2026 (three chunks): both trip-week notices and the whole recorded cluster are still printed, and the same read adds the items this record did not carry — the routine every-Sunday Marsaxlokk market diversions on Routes 81, 210 and 119 until about 17:00 (relevant to a Sunday 18 October outing), the Dingli diversion on Routes 52 and 201 until 30 June 2027, a Route 117 detour on Wednesday 14 October 12:00–17:00, Gozo-route detours across 12–15 October, and a feed-churn caution: an expired notice (Routes 203/280/31/41/42/48/N48, printed end date 1 July) still displays beside current ones, so a notice’s presence is not proof it runs and its absence is not proof a detour is lifted. On the Tuesday 13 October Attard-bound detours the printed stop omissions are Route 54 “from Fontaine through Aquilina” and Route 106 “from Wiji through Aquilina”, both 09:30–17:30. Third read 12 October 2026 (three chunks of the live feed plus the Route 186 page's own notice panel): both Route 186 notices are still displayed on both pages with the same wording — the October cluster (“weekly on Friday, Saturday from 7:00 PM to 12:00 AM, starting October 17”, omitting Gholja 2 → Targa toward Buġibba) and the separate older window ending “April 21” at 20:00–00:00 with identical stop-omission text — the Saqqajja (4627) stop closure is still listed, and no event-specific TQ, BLAST Arena Studios or Thunderpick notice has appeared.
